Synopsis:
    China is maintaining stable refined fuel export volumes in September vs August, with ~4 million metric tons of gasoline, diesel and jet fuel expected to be shipped. This follows Beijing's easing of export controls that were introduced in March after a US-Iran war disrupted Middle Eastern crude imports. Diesel export margins are strong (~$223/ton; Asia diesel crack ~$70/bbl), incentivising Chinese refiners. PetroChina and Sinopec hold >60% of allowances. A third quota batch is expected within a month. Rising Chinese exports are expected to cap regional Asian price gains.
